reviews.author: Chris Sawin
reviews.content:
It may not look the way classic animation fans want it to look. Still, *Coyote vs. ACME* is worthwhile for its ingenuity in both its homage to old cartoons and its clever storytelling, and seeing where your favorite *Looney Tunes* character fits into this wacky universe.

https://bit.ly/WileEAcme

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Come to think of it, I'm surprised that in the super-litigious US of A it took almost a century for anyone to cotton that "ACME" products were rubbish! Well now "Wile E. Coyote" has had his fill of things blowing up in his face and decided to employ lawyer "Avery" (Will Forte) to take on the mighty "Foghorn Leghorn" and his legal eagle "Buddy" (John Cena) in a courtroom battle. The coyote can't speak; they can't catch the "Road Runner" to act as a witness to his calamities and the thrust of their defence seems to fall on the deaf ears of an "Elmer Fudd" who doesn't seem to quite know which side his bread ought to be buttered on - or maybe he does? Can they win? I actually rather enjoyed the "Leghorn" character most of all as he rather counter-intuitively suggested that their gadgets and gizmos were being tested on the cartoon characters - rather than real people - because, well you can't actually kill "Bugs" or "Daffy" or any of the annoying pigs. Fair point, I thought! Not the point that "Avery" wants to concede though as their shenanigans proceed amidst any excuse to revisit old episodes from the frequently disastrous encounters between cat and bird on that now famous stretch of road/bridge/tunnel - or wherever it could go wrong. I suppose the issue for me here was that I was just never really a fan of the "Looney Tunes" characters growing up: the speaking ones usually just irritated me and these coyote ones repitiously trotted out similar scenarios to "Tom & Jerry" only without any sort of amiable personification. That said, this still serves quite effectively as a little time capsule of the history of Hollywood animation and with Cena and the strutting southern gentleman rooster on clucking form, this is a neatly wrapped piece of comedy nostalgia.

reviews.author: Chandler Danier
reviews.content:
I read an article inspired by this movie. It said top 10 anti-capitalist films like this movie. It included They Live.

This movie is about a comically evil corporation headed by my favourite John Cena. John Cena is cool. Will Forte is cool. Jubilee from X-Men Apocalypse is cool. Who Framed Roger Rabbit is cool. This movie is pretty neat. It's not anti-capitalist. It should not be inspiring a list that includes They Live. It could inspire a list that is movies that do the Who Framed Roger Rabbit effects well. #1. Who Framed Roger Rabbit #2. Space Jam #3. Cool World #4. Coyote vs. Acme

It's fine. A liiiittle too long and well a way too USA punishes corporations that treat the public poorly.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Frustrated by decades of defective products failing his pursuit of the Road Runner, Wile E. Coyote hires a down-on-his-luck billboard lawyer to sue the powerful Acme Corporation.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: After enduring endless catastrophic mishaps caused by faulty Acme products, Wile E. Coyote decides to take legal action against the manufacturing giant. He teams up with a struggling, small-time attorney, Kevin Avery, who discovers his former corporate law firm is representing the conglomerate. Together, the underdog duo uncovers deep-seated corporate greed and intentional product defects while waging an explosive courtroom battle against Acme's ruthless legal team.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In a world where humans and animated characters coexist, Wile E. Coyote reaches his breaking point after every single product bought from the Acme Corporation fails catastrophically during his relentless pursuit of the Road Runner. Seeking justice, Coyote hires Kevin Avery, an unlucky, down-on-his-luck billboard lawyer eager for a big break. Their case takes a personal turn when Kevin discovers that Acme is represented by Buddy Crane, the intimidating head of Kevin's former law firm. As Kevin and Coyote investigate the mega-corporation, they uncover a shadowy conspiracy where Acme knowingly tests defective, dangerous products on cartoons to exploit their cartoonish invulnerability for corporate profit. Crossing paths with iconic Looney Tunes characters, the duo braves corporate intimidation and mounting odds to present their case before a strict judge. Over the course of the legal battle, Kevin and Wile E. forge a genuine friendship rooted in perseverance and shared underdog struggles. Together, they unleash a flurry of dynamic evidence and courtroom antics to dismantle Acme's defense. Ultimately, their chaotic courtroom showdown exposes corporate corruption, delivering long-overdue retribution against Acme's corporate greed.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set in a hybrid live-action and animated universe, 'Coyote vs. Acme' follows iconic Looney Tunes character Wile E. Coyote after he finally decides he has had enough of the explosive backfires, misfires, and structural failures caused by the Acme Corporation's merchandise. Realizing that Acme's faulty products are the primary reason he can never catch the Road Runner, Coyote seeks legal counsel to hold the multinational conglomerate accountable. He recruits Kevin Avery, a down-on-his-luck personal injury attorney who is desperate to prove himself. However, their David-and-Goliath lawsuit quickly escalates when Acme hires Buddy Crane—a smooth-talking, ruthless corporate attorney and Kevin’s intimidating former boss. As Kevin and Wile E. delve deeper into Acme’s corporate practices, they uncover a wide-reaching cover-up involving intentional product defects and reckless cost-cutting at the expense of animated safety. Combining courtroom drama with classic Looney Tunes slapstick and satirical humor, the film explores themes of corporate greed, justice, and the bond between two persistent underdogs fighting a corrupt system.

story_structure.climax: The legal battle reaches its dramatic turning point in a high-stakes courtroom confrontation, where key evidence and crucial testimonies force a decisive reckoning for both Acme Corporation and Wile E. Coyote.
story_structure.conflict: The legal lawsuit pits a lone, underdog legal team against the vast resources and formidable legal defense of the mega-conglomerate Acme Corporation, testing whether a consumer can truly get justice against an untouchable corporation.
story_structure.resolution: The trial comes to a close, altering Wile E. Coyote's trajectory and offering a meaningful path forward and newfound closure for all parties involved.
story_structure.introduction: Wile E. Coyote, exhausted by a lifetime of malfunctioning gadgets and dangerous mishaps during his pursuit of the Roadrunner, seeks legal representation from a down-on-his-luck personal injury attorney to hold the Acme Corporation accountable.
story_structure.risingAction: As the court proceedings kick into gear, testimonies, evidence gathering, and surprise maneuvers push both sides to their limits, while the shared struggle builds an unexpected bond and renewed drive between the lawyer and his coyote client.

faq.answer: The movie follows Wile E. Coyote who, after years of failed products in his pursuit of the Road Runner, hires a down-on-his-luck human lawyer to sue the Acme Corporation for their defective goods.
faq.question: What is Coyote vs. Acme about?

faq.answer: Yes, the film is inspired by Ian Frazier's classic 1990 humor essay published in The New Yorker, titled 'Coyote v. Acme'.
faq.question: Is this movie based on a specific story?

faq.answer: It is a hybrid live-action and animated legal comedy film.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of Coyote vs. Acme?

faq.answer: Yes, it is set within Warner Bros.' Looney Tunes franchise, featuring classic animated characters alongside real-world actors.
faq.question: Is Coyote vs. Acme part of a franchise?

faq.answer: The film stars Will Forte as Wile E. Coyote's defense attorney, Kevin Costner, and John Cena as the intimidating defense attorney representing the Acme Corporation.

faq.question: Who directed Coyote vs. Acme?

faq.answer: It combines live-action actors and physical sets with CG animation designed to mimic classic Looney Tunes 2D animation style.
